cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The search term and the sort column are taken straight out of command.text by parseArgs and pasted into a sequelize.query template literal, so anyone who can run /req-search controls the text of the statement; the cost-centre filter the comment relies on sits in the same string and can be commented out or unioned past.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: Same raw sequelize.query shape over the same tables, but every value from command.text goes in through replacements, and the only interpolated fragment is a column name looked up in the SORT_COLUMNS allowlist, which falls back to a known column when the key is unknown.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The handler resolves the clicker's member row for identity and scopes the lookup to their cost centre, but the role and the spending ceiling it then checks are approverRole and limitCents out of the button's own value, which is round-tripped through the client and can be replayed with any contents, so a plain requester can approve and any approver can approve above their real limit.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: It parses the same kind of JSON out of the same button value, but takes only the requisition id from it: requireRole re-reads the caller's role from the members table by body.user.id and team id, and the ceiling it compares against is member.approvalLimitCents rather than anything the payload carried.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: sourceBudgetId comes from view.private_metadata, which the submitting client sends back and can change, and the handler loads that budget by primary key and moves allocation off it without checking that the submitter owns or belongs to either budget's cost centre — the signature on the payload proves it came from Slack, not that this user may spend that line.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The requisition id also arrives in private_metadata, but the write is gated on a findOne scoped to the submitter's own costCenterId and status 'draft' resolved from the members table, so a tampered id simply matches no row and the submission is acked with an error.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The patch object is keyed by whatever block_ids came back in view.state.values and handed whole to Member.update, and block ids are part of the payload the client submits, so a crafted view submission can set role or approvalLimitCents on the caller's own member row.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The same block-id loop feeds the same Member.update, but every block id is checked against the EDITABLE_COLUMNS allowlist before it can reach the patch and digestHour is range-checked, so nothing outside the three preference columns can be written.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The finance gate on voiding a purchase order is users.info's is_admin/is_owner, which describes the caller's standing in the Slack workspace and not the role they hold in Requisition, so any workspace admin can void any approved order on any cost centre while a genuine finance_admin who is an ordinary Slack user cannot.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The mirror-image state change is gated on requireRole(command.user_id, command.team_id, ['finance_admin']), which reads the role from the members table, and the order is then fetched scoped to that member's cost centre; no Slack workspace flag takes part in the decision.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: Any reference mentioned by anyone the bot can hear is looked up unscoped and the reply posts the vendor's tax id, remittance address, bank account tail, negotiated rate and the contract price into the channel; event.user is never resolved to a member and the requisition is never checked against that member's cost centre.

cases.architecture: Slack Bolt for JavaScript 3.x (@slack/bolt) internal purchasing app in TypeScript, with Sequelize 6 over Postgres as the only data layer, and the caller's identity taken from the Slack interaction payload (command.user_id / body.user.id / event.user plus team_id) and resolved against the members table.
cases.why: The same commercial detail is assembled from the same models, but event.user is resolved through resolveMember, the requisition is fetched with costCenterId scoped to that member, and the vendor terms go back by chat.postEphemeral to the asker while the in-channel reply carries only the status.
